title: Code Anatomy call 2: stack research and assembly from existing pieces
purpose: Find the existing software that Code Anatomy can be assembled from, so that implementation writes only glue and what no existing piece provides. The owner uses the result to start the implementation calls.
task: Read OWNER_ADDENDUM_2.md, OWNER_ADDENDUM.md and the locked spec v2 first. For every component slot S00-S20 in spec v2 section 13 and every adapter family in adapter-catalogue.md, survey the live web and GitHub for existing pieces, judge each against the slot's criteria with labelled evidence, and deliver one recommended assembly with a fallback per slot, a coverage matrix, a local smoke-test plan on the six pinned repositories, feedback on the spec, and ready-to-brief job files for implementation calls I01, I02 and I03. Work in this priority order so that a partial result is still usable: (1) the adopt-whole check and slots S01-S04, S14-S17; (2) slots S05-S13 and S18-S20; (3) the assembly plan and smoke test; (4) the three job files.

in: Check first whether an existing tool can be adopted whole (slot S00) for the mapper, for map delivery to an agent, or for checking a figure against code.
Survey candidates for every slot S00-S20 and for every row family (a) to (i) of the adapter catalogue.
Read each candidate's repository, licence file, releases, issues and documentation; run it if your environment allows.
Recommend one assembly: a primary and a fallback per slot, pinned versions, the implementation language or languages, data flow, adapters, and the inventory of code that is truly new.
Write a smoke-test plan the owner's side runs locally on Linux against the six pinned repositories in OWNER_ADDENDUM_2.md section 3.
Write ready-to-brief job files for implementation calls I01, I02 and I03 of spec/implementation-plan.md, using the chosen stack.
out: Changing the locked spec or either owner addendum. Disagreement goes in spec-feedback.md.
Claiming that anything ran unless it ran in this call.
Recommending as a primary any piece that needs a paid service, a hosted API or an account.

constraints: Spec v2 with OWNER_ADDENDUM.md and OWNER_ADDENDUM_2.md is authoritative; addendum 2 wins over the spec, and addendum 1 principles P1-P10 stay binding. Where research shows a clause is infeasible or better done another way, say so in spec-feedback.md with evidence; do not silently deviate.
Browse the live web and GitHub; do not rely on memory alone. List the searches made so the survey can be repeated.

Label every claim about a candidate RAN (you executed it in this call; give the command and the output), SOURCE (you opened the page or file; give URL and commit or access date) or UNVERIFIED (a README claim or recollection you did not check).
State the licence of every candidate as an SPDX identifier taken from its licence file, with the URL. Flag any term that restricts commercial use, private repositories, redistribution or bundling.

Give a determinism verdict for every candidate and say how it was judged: two runs compared byte for byte, a documented guarantee, or unknown. Say which output fields are known to vary (ordering, timestamps, absolute paths).

For every candidate state: whether it needs the project's dependencies installed, whether it needs the project to build, whether it executes project code, whether it needs the network at run time, and which operating systems it supports. For every precise resolver state which spec policy tier (NONE, PARTIAL, FULL_SANDBOX) it can run under.
Prefer maintained projects with releases or commits in 2025-2026. Flag archived, unmaintained or single-maintainer projects explicitly.
Reuse first: propose new code only for adapters and for capabilities no candidate provides, and say which.
Pin an exact version or commit for every recommended piece.
Write in plain, short sentences. Use tables for the candidate comparisons.
facts: The owner's goal, verbatim, is in OWNER_ADDENDUM.md section 1 and BRIEF.md section 1.

Spec v2 was produced by call 3 on 2026-10-12 and accepted by the owner's side with the changes in OWNER_ADDENDUM_2.md. Its schemas are valid JSON Schema draft 2020-12 and their example instances validate; this was checked locally.
The six phase 1 repositories are pinned to exact commits in OWNER_ADDENDUM_2.md section 3. Their licences, line counts and build status were not checked.

Anatomy is public at https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy . The supplied SKILL.md was copied from commit 689dcf966e63d92be10a5d593c6e19e10acd4422. Its LICENSE file is MIT. It states a need for Node.js 20.10+ and Chrome or Chromium.
Code Factory v2.2 section 17 lists the components it used and the alternatives it rejected for Python, with reasons and measurements.
The owner's machine is Linux x86_64 (Arch) with Node.js 26, Python 3 and Chromium installed.
hypotheses: Recalled by the preparing agent, unverified, and not a preference: candidate families may include tree-sitter grammars and tag queries; SCIP or LSIF indexers; language servers driven headless; universal-ctags; code property graph tools such as Joern; Kythe; Glean; CodeQL; stack-graphs; ast-grep and Semgrep; language detectors such as Linguist or enry; SBOM and dependency tools such as Syft or cdxgen; sandboxes such as bubblewrap, nsjail, gVisor or rootless containers; OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation; and repository-map tools built for LLM agents.
Some of these may be archived, licence-restricted, non-deterministic in output order, or need a project build. Check each; do not assume.
A complete off-the-shelf tool that meets the spec may or may not exist.
Few existing tools may cover agent frameworks (prompts, tools, model calls, handoffs, MCP). If none does, say so and size the new adapter code.
assumptions: The responder can browse the public web and GitHub.
The responder may or may not be able to install and run candidates. Either is acceptable if the evidence label is honest.

requirements.requirement: Adopt-whole check (slot S00). Survey existing tools that already map a multi-language codebase for an LLM agent, that produce flows or architecture views from code, or that verify a diagram against code. Give each a verdict against spec v2's hard rules H01-H12: ADOPT WHOLE, USE AS COMPONENT or REJECT.

acceptance.condition: stack-research.md has an adopt-whole section with at least 12 tools surveyed, each with URL, licence, last release or commit date, the hard rules it meets and fails, the verdict and the evidence label.

requirements.requirement: Survey candidates for every slot S01-S20. For each candidate record every field that spec v2 section 13 requires of a slot report, plus the fields required by this job's constraints.

acceptance.condition: Every slot id S01-S20 appears in stack-research.md and candidates.json with at least 3 candidates where 3 exist, or a statement of how the search was made if fewer exist. Every required field is filled or marked UNVERIFIED.

requirements.requirement: Coverage matrix. For each of the six phase 1 ecosystems and for each adapter family (a) to (i) of the adapter catalogue: which pieces of the recommended assembly cover it, which node and edge kinds they can emit, which evidence kind and policy tier that needs, and what stays an open end. Add rows for at least ten further languages outside the six, showing what the generic syntax adapter alone reaches.

acceptance.condition: stack-research.md has the matrix with one row per phase 1 ecosystem, one per adapter family, and at least ten further languages. Each row names the pieces, the kinds emitted, the policy tier needed, the known gaps and the evidence label. Agent-framework coverage is shown per framework named in the adapter catalogue.

requirements.requirement: Recommend one assembly: a primary and a fallback per slot with pinned versions; the implementation language or languages for the mapper, the query engine and the verifier, with the reason; the data flow between pieces; each adapter and what it converts; how byte-identical output is preserved end to end; the install footprint; and the inventory of code that is truly new with a rough size for each item.

acceptance.condition: assembly-plan.md names a primary and a fallback for every slot S01-S20, shows the data flow from repository to canonical map to query page to brief to binding check, lists every adapter, and lists the new code items with sizes. Every recommended primary meets the slot's must-have criteria, or the miss is recorded in spec-feedback.md.

requirements.requirement: Check the assembly against every gate G1-G11 in spec v2 section 12: state from evidence whether the gate is expected to be met, and name the measurement to run where it is unknown.

acceptance.condition: assembly-plan.md has one row per gate G1-G11 with EXPECTED MET, EXPECTED MISSED or UNKNOWN, the evidence with its label, and the measurement to run for each UNKNOWN.

requirements.requirement: Write a smoke-test plan the owner's side runs locally on Linux: exact commands to install the pinned primaries for slots S01-S03 and S14-S15 without root where possible, check out the six pinned repositories at their commits, run the pieces twice on each named subfolder, compare the outputs byte for byte, and count files classified, declarations found and references resolved. Give the expected result of each step. Do not present it as run unless it ran.

acceptance.condition: assembly-plan.md has a smoke-test section with copy-paste commands, the six repositories with the commits from OWNER_ADDENDUM_2.md, the pass condition of each step, and a statement of which steps were or were not run in this call.

requirements.requirement: List every clause of spec v2 or of the two addenda that the research shows to be infeasible, costly or better done differently, with the evidence and a proposed amendment. If there is none, say so.

acceptance.condition: spec-feedback.md lists each affected clause by document and section, the evidence with its label and the proposed amendment, or states that no clause is affected.

requirements.requirement: Write three ready-to-brief job files, for implementation calls I01 (frozen inventory and canonical identity), I02 (generic grammar and reference accounting) and I03 (deterministic graph engine, scopes and brief) of the supplied implementation plan, in the format of the supplied example job and using the recommended assembly. The supplied jobs-as-returned files are too thin and are examples of what not to deliver. Each job must ask for source code and tests as deliverables, name exact file paths, and give each requirement an acceptance the owner's side can check by running a command.

acceptance.condition: jobs/I01.job.json, jobs/I02.job.json and jobs/I03.job.json each contain project, title, purpose, task, scope, constraints, requirements, deliverables, sources and stop_condition; have at least six requirements each with an acceptance condition that names a command and its expected result; use only the acceptance methods review, exists or json-schema and the reviewers operator, terminal or mechanical (never review with mechanical; json-schema only with evidence results); and name as sources only files supplied to this call or delivered by it.
candidates.json is present in the outputs ZIP.

requirements.requirement: Report the adopt-whole verdict and the chosen primary and fallback per slot in the results object.

acceptance.condition: The results object validates against the result schema: a summary, an adopt-whole verdict, and one entry per slot with primary and fallback.

deliverables.description: The survey: searches made, adopt-whole check, candidates per slot with labelled evidence, licences, determinism verdicts, dependency and build needs, and the coverage matrix.

Machine-readable list of every candidate: slot, name, URL, licence, pinned version, last activity, verdict, evidence label, determinism verdict, needs-dependencies flag, needs-build flag, executes-project-code flag, policy tier.
The recommended assembly: primary and fallback per slot, implementation language, data flow, adapters, new-code inventory, gate check and the local smoke-test plan.
Clauses of spec v2 or the addenda that the research challenges, with evidence and proposed amendments.
Ready-to-brief job file for implementation call I01, frozen inventory and canonical identity.
Ready-to-brief job file for implementation call I02, generic grammar and reference accounting.
Ready-to-brief job file for implementation call I03, deterministic graph engine, scopes and brief.

sources.role: Read first. Binding; wins over spec v2. On-demand rendering of deep levels (A1-A9), the six pinned phase 1 repositories, corrected worked-example anchors, and what was not accepted from call 3.
Binding. The owner's clarified goal verbatim and principles P1-P10 that spec v2 implements.
The original brief. Owner decisions D1-D7 remain binding. Background for the rest.

The locked spec v2. Authoritative under the two addenda. Section 13 defines slots S00-S20 and what each slot report must record; section 12 defines gates G1-G11; sections 1-11 define what the pieces must produce.
The adapter targets by family (a) to (i): frameworks, formats and protocols to cover. Each row needs an existing piece or sized new code.
Why each spec v2 decision was made and what measurement would overturn it. Use it when writing spec-feedback.md.
The call 3 responder's case against spec v2. Contrary evidence to weigh, especially on cost, sandbox risk and generic-grammar coverage.
The canonical map format every recommended piece must be adapted to.
The figure binding format the verifier checks. OWNER_ADDENDUM_2.md A8 adds a portal state to it.
A valid instance of the map schema (hand-written reduction of the MCP weather server). Shows the target output shape for the assembly.
The ordered implementation calls I01-I10. The three job files you write are for I01, I02 and I03.
Call 3's job file for I01, not accepted: too thin. An example of what not to deliver for requirement R8.
The expired Python-only predecessor. Section 17 holds its component choices, rejected alternatives and measurements; treat them as dated evidence to re-check, not as current fact.
Anatomy's SKILL.md at commit 689dcf9: the drawing skill the assembly must feed and sit beside, including its runtime needs.
Format reference that jobs/I01.job.json, jobs/I02.job.json and jobs/I03.job.json must follow.

stop_condition: Deliver all seven files. If time or length runs short, finish in the priority order given in the task and report PARTIAL, naming in limitations which slots or files are thin or missing. Mark anything that could not be checked UNVERIFIED rather than guessing.
